known.title: tagPublished reads exit status 2 of git ls-remote as an absent tag without --exit-code, so a reachable origin always reports the tag as published and every re-cut is refused.
known.summary: tagPublished (scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:480-499) asks origin with `git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/<tag>` (line 491). It discards the output with stdio 'ignore' (line 493). It returns false only on exit status 2 (line 495), and it returns true on exit status 0 (line 498). The command does not pass --exit-code. The official page says: '--exit-code: Exit with status "2" when no matching refs are found in the remote repository. Usually the command exits with status "0" to indicate it successfully talked with the remote repository, whether it found any matching refs.' (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-remote#Documentation/git-ls-remote.txt---exit-code). Thus status 2 never occurs. A reachable origin without the tag gives status 0, and tagPublished returns true. scripts/AGENTS.md:29 says that tagPublished 'answers whether a release tag is already published', and the plan says that the check keeps its order, its result, and its refusal text unchanged (Decisions, step:closed_tag_check). The release refuses a same-version run when tagPublished returns true (scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:293-295). Scenario: tag-CI fails for plan-lifecycle--v0.6.1. The author runs the printed recovery (scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:369-372): delete the tag locally and on origin, then run `node scripts/release.mjs --plugin plan-lifecycle 0.6.1`. No local tag exists, origin lists nothing, git ls-remote exits 0, and the release stops with 'already released: plan-lifecycle v0.6.1'. Plan acceptance A1 (`node scripts/release.mjs --plugin plan-lifecycle 0.6.0 --dry-run` while 0.6.0 has no tag) fails the same way. So the re-cut path that the plan describes can never run. Checked locally with git 2.53.0: origin had only docks--v1.0.0 and the clone had no local tag. `git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/docks--v9.9.9` printed nothing and exited 0, and with --exit-code it exited 2. tagPublished('docks--v9.9.9') of this adapter returned true. The test fixture stubs tagPublished, so the suite does not catch the defect.

known.title: The adapter contract restores the saved Git environment with Object.assign, so a key that was unset becomes the string 'undefined' and later git calls in the test process fail.
known.summary: testReleaseAdapterGitContracts (scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs:2568-2588) saves the five isolation keys in `inherited` (line 2581). A key that was unset before is saved as undefined. The finally block restores them with `Object.assign(process.env, inherited)` (line 2586). The Node documentation says: 'Assigning a property on process.env will implicitly convert the value to a string.' Its example shows `env.test = undefined; console.log(env.test); // => 'undefined'`, and it says: 'Use delete to delete a property from process.env.' (https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#processenv). So an unset key becomes the string 'undefined' and does not become unset again. The comment at line 2573 says 'Every key is restored below', and the plan says that the test restores every prior value (Decisions, step:ambient_config). Git rejects the leaked values. With GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=undefined, git prints 'error: bogus count in GIT_CONFIG_COUNT' and 'fatal: unable to parse command-line config' and exits 128. With GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=undefined, git prints "fatal: bad boolean environment value 'undefined' for 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM'" and exits 128. GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM then name a file called 'undefined'. Scenario: a developer shell has none of these keys set, which is the usual case. Checked locally (Node v24.22.1, git 2.53.0): `env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM node scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs --unit` with an exit hook showed GIT_CONFIG_COUNT="undefined" and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="undefined" after the suite, and `git status --porcelain` spawned in that process exited 128. Every later git spawn that inherits process.env fails. The shim matrix that runs next passes only because it sets the same keys again.

known.title: The already-released test passes a string as the second argument of assert.rejects, so Node uses it as the failure message and any rejection passes.
known.summary: The already-released case (scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs:995-1005) calls assert.rejects with the template string `already released: ${recutPlugin.name} v${recutVersion}` as its second argument (line 1004). The Node documentation for assert.rejects says: 'error cannot be a string. If a string is provided as the second argument, then error is assumed to be omitted and the string will be used for message instead. This can lead to easy-to-miss mistakes.' (https://nodejs.org/api/assert.html#assertrejectsasyncfn-error-message). So the assertion accepts any rejection and does not check the refusal text. A RegExp or an object with `message` would check it. The plan requires the suite to assert the `already released` refusal (step:closed_tag_check Done when, acceptance A5). Scenario: a change makes the same-version path reject with another error before or instead of the refusal, for example a TypeError. Checked locally (Node v24.22.1): with the refusal at scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:294 changed to `throw new TypeError(`plugin ${plugin.name} manifest is unreadable`)`, `node scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs --unit` still exited 0. With a RegExp matcher in the same place, the run failed with an AssertionError that expected /already released: plan-lifecycle v0.6.0/.
